title: Homeland Security and ICE funding (2026)
summary: In January 2026 the Senate split the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) bill off a six-bill FY2026 funding package and passed the other five. The separate DHS bill (H.R. 7147) then failed repeated Senate votes, leading to a partial DHS shutdown that ended April 30, 2026 with a version that left out ICE funding. In June 2026 the Senate passed S. 2, a reconciliation bill providing $70 billion for DHS, CBP and ICE immigration enforcement.

summary.text: Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026 This bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) through May 22, 2026. It is known as a continuing resolution (CR) and ends the partial DHS shutdown that began on February 14, 2026, due to a lapse in appropriations for DHS. The CR generally funds most DHS agencies and programs at the FY2025 levels through the earlier of May 22, 2026, or the enactment of the FY2026 DHS appropriations act. The bill also requires specified funds to be used to provide back pay, in accordance with current law, to federal employees affected by a government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations. Finally, the bill ratifies and approves certain obligations that were incurred during a government shutdown, including obligations incurred to maintain the essential level of activity to protect life and property and bring about an orderly termination of government functions.

Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 This bill provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026 and provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) through February 13, 2026. It also extends various expiring programs and authorities. Specifically, the bill includes 5 of the 12 regular FY2026 appropriations bills: the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026; the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026;  the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026; the Financial Services and General Government Appropriations Act, 2026; and the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026. The departments, agencies, and activities funded in the bill include the Department of Defense, the Department of Labor, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Education, the Department of Transportation, the Department of Housing and Urban Development,  the Department of the Treasury, the Executive Office of the President, the judiciary, the District of Columbia, the Department of State and related programs, the administration and oversight of foreign assistance programs,   bilateral economic assistance, international security assistance, multilateral assistance, export and investment assistance, and severa

Secure America Act This act provides $70 billion in funding to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) through FY2029 for immigration enforcement, border security, and related activities. It is known as a reconciliation bill and includes legislation submitted by certain congressional committees pursuant to provisions in the FY2026 congressional budget resolution ( S. Con. Res. 33 ) that directed the committees to submit legislation to the House or Senate Budget Committee that will increase the deficit. (Reconciliation bills are considered by Congress using expedited legislative procedures that prevent a filibuster and restrict amendments in the Senate.) TITLE I--COMMITTEE ON HOMELAND SECURITY AND GOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS (Sec. 101) This section provides funding for CBP to hire, pay, train, and equip Border Patrol agents and Border Patrol support personnel to conduct functions other than immigration enforcement and customs functions. The funds provided by this section may not be used to recruit, hire, or train personnel for the duties of processing coordinators after October 31, 2028. (Sec. 102) This section provides funding to ICE for (1) hiring, paying, training, and equipping Homeland Security Investigations (HIS) agents and support personnel; and (2) other necessary expenses for HSI’s mission support and operations and maintenance. promises.name: Edward J. Markey
promises.quote: I will not support any funding deal that puts money in the hands of Stephen Miller, Kristi Noem, and this violent agency.
promises.promise: Said he will not support any funding deal that funds ICE under its current leadership.

promises.name: Pete Ricketts
promises.quote:
It is my priority to pass the remaining regular appropriations bills before the January 30 deadline to provide certainty for our military and essential services.

I will continue to support DHS funding to ensure our immigration laws are enforced and Nebraskans are safe.
promises.promise: Said he will continue to support DHS funding.

promises.name: Gary C. Peters
promises.quote: That is why I will be voting no on [the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026] unless--unless--DHS funding is stripped out or unless critical reforms are incorporated into the bill.
promises.promise: Said he will vote no on the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 unless DHS funding is stripped or reforms added.

promises.name: Richard J. Durbin
promises.quote: I will not vote to fund the illegal DHS and ICE operations that terrorize Chicago, Minneapolis, and many other communities.
promises.promise: Said he will not vote to fund DHS and ICE operations he described as illegal.

promises.name: Gary C. Peters
promises.quote: I will be voting no on the DHS funding bill because it lacks necessary reforms to immigration enforcement.
promises.promise: Said he will vote no on the DHS funding bill lacking immigration-enforcement reforms.

promises.name: Ben Ray Luján
promises.quote: Kristi Noem and Donald Trump’s ICE is out of control and terrorizing our communities. With multiple deadly shootings of American citizens by federal agents in Minnesota and no accountability, I will not support an appropriations bill that funds DHS without real oversight, transparency, and consequences. President Trump, Kristi Noem, and Stephen Miller are making our communities and all Americans less safe. Enough is enough.
promises.promise: Said he will not support a DHS appropriations bill without real oversight, transparency, and consequences.

promises.name: Tina Smith
promises.quote: My power is my vote as a Senator, and I’m not voting to send an extra dollar in funding to ICE/DHS while they trample on Minnesotans like this.
promises.promise: Said she will not vote to send additional funding to ICE/DHS amid enforcement actions in Minnesota.

statements.name: Tina Smith
statements.quote: Tomorrow, Republicans in the Senate are going to force through a partisan bill to give ICE and Customs and Border Protection almost $70 billion, all because they have refused to do anything to rein in the abuses of ICE--abuses that destroyed trust, killed American citizens, and ripped Minnesota families apart.

statements.name: Richard J. Durbin
statements.quote:
I voted no on Markwayne Mullin’s nomination to be DHS Secretary.

I will not vote to install another yes-man to enable Donald Trump.

statements.name: Dan Sullivan
statements.quote: So I am very hopeful that we are going to have a strong bipartisan vote for our colleague Senator Markwayne Mullin to move forward as the Secretary of Homeland Security.

statements.name: Roger Marshall
statements.quote: In a second, I am going to offer a clean 2-week CR to fully fund DHS.

statements.name: John W. Hickenlooper
statements.quote: This morning, I voted against a government funding that would have handed billions of dollars to DHS.

statements.name: Gary C. Peters
statements.quote: I voted no on the funding bill today because we need serious reforms to require @DHSgov immigration enforcement operations to be conducted safely and responsibly. I urge our Republican colleagues to let us vote to fund the rest of the government and work with us to rein in DHS.
